# gaba_excites

> A browser simulator of current-clamp recording from a cortical
> regular-spiking pyramidal neuron, for teaching excitability. It runs
> entirely on the reader's machine: no server, no upload, no analytics.

This is a hand-maintained plain-text summary of https://gaba.tonydefazio.com/
for readers that do not run JavaScript. The full account, with every equation,
is at https://gaba.tonydefazio.com/methods (static HTML), and every source,
with what was taken from it, is at https://gaba.tonydefazio.com/lit.
A plain introduction to action potentials, by the author, for readers with no
background, is at https://gaba.tonydefazio.com/explainer (a first draft).

## What it does

- Five models, chosen from a menu:
  - the regular-spiking (RS) pyramidal cell of Pospischil et al. 2008
    (Biol Cybern 99:427, doi:10.1007/s00422-008-0263-8; ModelDB 123623): one
    compartment, Traub INa and IKd, slow M-type IK for adaptation;
  - the fast-spiking interneuron of the same paper and ModelDB entry
    (sIN_template): the same INa and IKd, twice the K+ density, no M current;
    it does not adapt, and like the pyramidal cell it is checked spike for
    spike against NEURON running the original mechanisms;
  - the low-threshold-spike (LTS) pyramidal cell of the same ModelDB entry
    (sPYr_template with demo_PY_LTS.hoc; originally Destexhe, Contreras &
    Steriade 2001, Neurocomputing 38-40:555, doi:10.1016/S0925-2312(01)00348-4):
    the pyramidal cell's INa, IKd and IM plus Huguenard's T-type ICa and
    Destexhe's calcium shell, checked spike for spike against NEURON. Held at
    -64 mV (60 pA) it fires on release from a hyperpolarizing step (rebound);
    from its own rest at -84 mV it does not, and bursts on depolarization;
  - the mouse GnRH neuron of Adams et al. 2018 (J Neurosci 38:1249,
    doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.2988-17.2017), negative-feedback parameter set:
    Markov INaF, INaP, IA, IK, T-type and HVA ICa, IS, Ih, IKCa, calcium pool;
  - the mouse pancreatic beta cell of Bertram et al. 2004 (Biophys J 87:3074,
    doi:10.1529/biophysj.104.049262), the Dual Oscillator Model: IK, ICa,
    IK(Ca), IK(ATP), cytosolic and ER calcium, oscillating glycolysis and
    calcium-slowed ATP production. It fires on its own in glucose, so it runs
    on the oscilloscope only, with a glucose control (the glucokinase rate) and
    the paper's patterns;
  - the human pancreatic beta cell of Riz, Braun & Pedersen 2014 (PLoS Comput
    Biol 10:e1003389, doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003389), on Pedersen 2010
    (Biophys J 99:3200, doi:10.1016/j.bpj.2010.09.004): INa, L-, P/Q- and
    T-type ICa, IKv, IBK (driven by the Ca2+ current), ISK, IHERG, IK(ATP), and
    a bath GABA_A conductance reversing at -40 mV, with submembrane and
    cytosolic calcium. Its voltage-gated currents come from voltage-clamp
    recordings of human beta cells (Braun et al. 2008). It spikes on its own
    at about 6 Hz; GABA excites it;
  - the squid giant axon of Hodgkin & Huxley 1952 (J Physiol 117:500,
    doi:10.1113/jphysiol.1952.sp004764): INa and IK only, on a space-clamped
    10 000 um^2 patch (100 pF, so 100 pA = 1 uA/cm^2), with a temperature
    control (Q10 = 3, default 6.3 degC). No propagation.
- The user sets whole-cell passive properties — the leak conductance gL in nS,
  Cm (sets cell size; channel densities stay fixed) and holding current — and
  electrode properties: series resistance, bridge balance, pipette capacitance.
- Currents show in pA or, with a switch, as density in pA/pF (= uA/cm^2 at
  1 uF/cm^2), each converted by its own cell's Cm. Display only: the
  simulation and the CSV stay in pA.
- Runs families of current steps (first/increment/count, or any list) and
  reports rheobase with the Vm it was measured from (refinable to 1 pA;
  the human beta cell, which fires on its own, from −70 mV), spike threshold (where dV/dt
  reaches the cell's own criterion: 10 V/s for the cortical cells and the
  squid axon, 1 V/s for GnRH, 0.5 V/s for the human beta cell; a switch on
  the phase plot tries 0.5, 1, 2, 10 and 20 V/s),
  AP peak and half-width, input resistance (measured, never set: from the
  steady-state I–V at rest and from the hyperpolarizing steps), and the F–I curve (mean and initial
  rate); F–I curves can be pinned for comparison and exported as CSV.
- A lab notebook records runs with titles and notes and downloads a
  self-contained HTML report (tables, figures, an auto-written methods
  paragraph, threshold at 0.5, 1, 2, 10 and 20 V/s). The report embeds its runs as
  JSON and loads back in. Everything stays in the browser.
- An oscilloscope mode runs the same cell continuously, with every control
  live and a repeating current pulse on top of the holding current. It uses
  the same integrator; unchanged, it reproduces a step-protocol sweep sample
  for sample. Readouts (firing rate, mean Vm) are measured on true Vm.
- A voltage-clamp mode holds the cell at a command and records the current,
  with the series resistance in the loop (0 is an ideal clamp). Protocols:
  activation (I-V), steady-state inactivation, tail currents, recovery from
  inactivation, or user-edited segments with one varied in voltage or
  duration. No curve is drawn from the model's equations: the user chooses
  what to take in a window (peak + or -, max |I|, mean, cursor), and the I-V,
  G-V or availability curve and a Boltzmann fit come from those
  measurements, made on the
  recorded current (filtered, with noise). Channels can be blocked one by one,
  in either clamp. Checked against NEURON's SEClamp on the pyramidal cell:
  every sample within 10 pA and 0.01 mV, near-ideal and at 2 MOhm.
- In the oscilloscope, an audio monitor (hiss with a pop per spike, or a tone
  whose pitch follows Vm, four octaves over -90..+40 mV). The app opens in an
  "Old school" look, in both modes: a dark instrument panel with knurled knobs
  for every control, and in the oscilloscope a green-phosphor tube with
  persistence and analog meters with needle ballistics. A switch turns it off.
- A siren flags unphysiologic drive, using criteria taken from the cell
  itself: spike failure (no overshoot, or depolarization block above -30 mV
  for 50 ms), Vm beyond the reversal potentials in play, or injected current
  more than 10x the published cell's rheobase from its holding current.
- Two kinds of noise: recording noise (filtered Gaussian plus mains hum, on
  the recorded trace only) and membrane noise (an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck current
  the cell feels).
- Adds conductance-based glutamate (E = 0 mV) and GABA-A PSCs (E_GABA
  variable; default -80 mV for the pyramidal cell and -36.5 mV for the GnRH
  neuron, as measured by gramicidin perforated patch in DeFazio et al. 2002,
  Mol Endocrinol 16:2872; the GnRH neuron's GABA PSC defaults to the measured
  10 ms decay and ~1 nS peak of Jaime et al. 2026, J Neuroendocrinol
  38:e70144), each with rate, peak conductance, rise and decay,
  Poisson or regular timing, from a seeded generator.

## Validation

Pyramidal cell: spike counts match NEURON 9.0.2 running the original ModelDB
mechanisms exactly for steps of 500–1500 pA, and every spike time agrees
within 0.2 ms (dt = 0.01 ms).

GnRH neuron: transcribed from the paper (no public code exists to compare
against). It reproduces what the paper reports: -6 pA holds it at -70 mV, and
500 ms steps of 0/6/12/18/24/30 pA give 0/0/0/1/4/6 spikes, as in its Fig. 7F.

Squid axon: spike counts match NEURON 9.0.2's built-in hh mechanism (rate
tables off, E_L -54.387 mV) exactly on 21 steps at 6.3 and 18.5 degC, every
spike within 0.01 ms. Rheobase 225 pA (2.25 uA/cm^2, 800 ms step); no slow
firing: between 600 and 700 pA it goes from one or two spikes to 59 Hz;
release from -300 pA (3.3 mV below rest) fires an anode-break spike. Checked
against the 1952 paper as well: its rate functions and Table 3 constants
exactly (after the sign change Vm = -(V + 65)), every membrane action
potential in its Table 4 (e.g. 15 mV shock at 6.3 degC: spike 105.4 mV, max
rise 310 V/s; the paper: 105.4, 311) and the threshold of Fig. 12 (7 mV fires,
6 mV does not); voltage clamp matches the paper's clamped-step solution
within 1%. methods.html#checked tabulates how every model was checked.

Beta cell: transcribed from the paper, the PFK rate law from the authors' code.
It reproduces what the paper reports: glycolysis alone oscillates at R_GK 0.2
(about 5 min) and not at 0.4, and is bistable at 0.3; the whole cell bursts
every 32.4 s at R_GK 0.4 (the paper: about 30 s) and gives the compound,
accordion, glycolytic and subthreshold patterns of its Figs. 5-8. The authors'
equations integrated by a stiff solver give 30.3-31.6 s from the same start.

Human beta cell: transcribed from both papers. With Pedersen 2010's settings
it fires at 4.62 Hz between -8.5 and -67.9 mV (the paper: 4.6 Hz, -8 and
-68 mV), at 7.06 Hz with HERG blocked (7 Hz), and TTX lengthens the interval
from 216 to 313 ms (217 to 312). With Riz et al. 2014's settings, 100 uM GABA
on a silent cell gives a single spike and a plateau at -44 mV (the paper:
~-45 mV), and 10 uM speeds a spiking cell from 5.7 to 7.7 Hz. The authors'
equations integrated by a stiff solver give interspike intervals within 0.5%
of the port in nine configurations. Spikes are counted at -30 mV for this cell
(they peak between -7 and -28 mV), -20 mV for the others.

## The result it is named for

On the published pyramidal cell, with clock-like GABA (200 Hz, 3 nS, 0.5/10 ms),
rheobase is 561 pA without GABA, 765 pA with E_GABA = -80 mV, 628 pA at
-60 mV (GABA depolarizes the cell yet still inhibits, by shunting), 560 pA at
-50 mV (neutral), and 458 pA at -35 mV (excitatory). The crossover is about
11 mV below spike threshold.

## Dynamic clamp

On the amplifier, in current clamp: a conductance added to the cell or, with a
negative value, subtracted. Kv4 is the transient K+ conductance of Mendonca et
al. 2016 (eLife 5:e16475), which Mendonca et al. 2018 (J Physiol 596:885)
injected into arcuate kisspeptin neurons; the dose is their peak conductance
at 0 mV (41.6% of the maximal conductance). The reversal, -90 mV, and the
-90 mV start of that test step are assumptions: the 2018 paper states neither.
The clamp is ideal (reads true Vm, no electrode or delay). A voltage-gated
conductance partly open at rest is also a leak (1.4% of this Kv4 at -70 mV),
so the panel shows rest and input resistance with the clamp on and off, and
can inject, in place of the Kv4, the plain leak with its steady current and
slope at rest, or the Kv4 with that leak subtracted (gating only). On the GnRH
cell, 8 nS (0.4 nS/pF): rest -67.5 to -69.9 mV, Rin 506 to 307 MOhm, rheobase
15.8 to 43.1 pA; its leak alone 31.0 pA, its gating alone 22.2 pA. The leak's
share of the rheobase change is a little over half there and 40% on the
pyramidal cell: it depends on the cell. Subtracting 6 nS leaves the GnRH cell
with no stable rest.

## Limits

One compartment; no Ih, calcium currents, NMDA, GABA-B, plasticity or
chloride dynamics; current clamp only; the published cell's Rin (32 MOhm) is
a high-conductance, in-vivo-like value.

## Source

https://github.com/syncytium2/gaba_excites (MIT). A command line
(`node scripts/fi.ts`) runs the same code without a browser.
